ukmt-cayley-2016-c1.prompt: How many three-digit multiples of $9$ consist only of odd digits?

ukmt-cayley-2016-c3.prompt:
All the telephone numbers in Georgetown have six digits and each of them begins with the digits $81$. Kate finds the scrap of paper shown, with part of Jenny's telephone number on it (the scrap shows the digits 1018 printed sideways, so it can be read either way up: as $1018$ or as $8101$).

How many different possibilities are there for Jenny's telephone number?

ukmt-cayley-2016-c4.prompt:
The diagram shows an equilateral triangle $ABC$ and two squares $AWXB$ and $AYZC$.

Prove that triangle $AXZ$ is equilateral.
ukmt-cayley-2016-c4.answer: $\angle ZAX=60^\circ$ and $AZ=AX$ (equal diagonals of equal squares), so $AXZ$ is equilateral.

ukmt-cayley-2016-c5.answer: No: some row and some column contain neither $4$ nor $8$, so each must contain both $2$ and $6$, but $2$ and $6$ share only one cell.

ukmt-cayley-2016-c6.prompt:
The diagram shows two regular heptagons $ABCDEFG$ and $APQRSTU$. The vertex $P$ lies on the side $AB$ (and hence $U$ lies on the side $GA$). Also, $Q$ lies on $OB$, where $O$ is the centre of the larger heptagon.

Prove that $AB=2AP$.
